posts.title: The Diary of Wiska Wildflower: The New School by Harriet Muncaster – Book Review
posts.description: About The first book in an exciting new series from the creator of Isadora Moon, Harriet Muncaster. Told in diary format and packed with beautiful full-colour illustrations, this is the enchanting story of Wiska Wildflower and her search for friendship at Inkcap”s Academy. – Goodreads Thoughts I can’t get over how absolutely adorable the artwork is in this book. It is the perfect series for anyone with a love of fairytales and those with a creative spirit. It’s cute, and cozy artwork is accompanied by, and a great story written from Wiska’s perspective as diary entries and highlights the importance of staying true to yourself instead of trying desperately to fit in. Through Wiska’s experiences at her new school, readers are shown that the types of people we choose to be friends with should be those who treat us with kindness and respect back, and who encourage us to be ourselves. posts.title: Marble Hall Murders by Anthony Horowitz – Novel Review
posts.description: About Editor Susan Ryeland has left her Greek island, her hotel, and her Greek boyfriend Andreas in search of a new life back in England. Freelancing for Causton Books, she’s working on the manuscript of a novel, Pund’s Last Case , by a young author named Eliot Crace, a continuation of the popular Alan Conway series. Susan is surprised to learn that Eliot is the grandson of legendary children’s author Marian Crace, who died some fifteen years ago—murdered, Elliot insists, by poison. The deeper Susan reads, the more it becomes clear that the clues leading to the truth of Marian Crace’s death are hidden within this Atticus Pund mystery. – Goodreads Thoughts I had a ton of fun reading this novel, and managed to finish it before the first episode aired. posts.title: The Other Side of Perfect by Melanie Florence and Richard Scrimger – Book Review
posts.description: About Cody’s home life is terrifying. He walks on eggshells around his father, never knowing when he’ll lose his temper. Autumn is a wealthy girl from an Indigenous family, who has found herself in with the popular crowd even though the group she’s trying to fit in with, forces her to keep her hobbies and interests a secret. It’s getting harder for her to maintain her picture perfect image. One night, Autumn comes across Cody, face down in the laneway behind her house. All Cody knows is that he can’t take another encounter with his father like the one he just narrowly escaped. He can’t go home. But he doesn’t have anywhere else to go. When Autumn agrees to let him hide out in her dad’s art studio, the two slowly learn to trust one another, and discover a community neither of them knew they needed.
